title: Incremental typed stream consumers with pydantic v2 + dataclass fallback
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Deliver a developer-friendly, incremental parsing and hydration layer for streaming LLM responses that: (1) exposes a simple async iterator/Sync iterator API for typed model consumption, (2) prefers pydantic v2 for runtime validation and conversion, (3) falls back to lightweight dataclasses for constrained environments or when pydantic is not installed, and (4) preserves retry/resume semantics for partially-consumed streams.
acceptance_criteria: AsyncIterator and SyncIterator APIs exist and documented with examples
Typed model hydration uses pydantic v2 by default and dataclass fallback when pydantic import fails
Streaming parser exposes checkpoint markers that allow at-most-once resume from last complete token boundary
Unit tests covering backpressure, interrupted streams, and retry-resume semantics
Performance regression < 8% for common gen sizes compared to untyped streaming baseline
Docs + cookbook example published in SDK examples repo and linked in Quickstart
implementation_notes: Design an incremental JSON parser that emits full schema objects only when closed (to avoid exposing partial objects to callers)
Expose a small compatibility shim: from_sdk import TypedStreamConsumer with parameters: model_schema, max_buffer_tokens, prefer_pydantic

When pydantic import succeeds, use model_schema.parse_obj / pydantic.BaseModel.validate to ensure strict field types; otherwise, use dataclass.from_dict lightweight conversion with optional soft validation
Retry semantics: attach a stream_cursor token to outgoing requests; on server-side transient failure, client replays upstream until cursor and resumes hydration from last completed object checkpoint
Backpressure: provide a low-level callback for callers to signal slow consumers (pause read from socket) and expose an internal queue with configurable max_items
Edge-case: handle mixed chunk boundaries where a JSON object spans multiple SSE/chunks; ensure checkpoint only at end-of-object matching schema
Include integration test harness recording real model outputs (small/medium/long) and assert schema invariants under simulated network interruption
design_decisions: Prefer pydantic v2 for feature parity with typed SDK work and better performance; avoid pydantic v1 compatibility shims
Fallback to dataclasses reduces runtime dependency surface for constrained customers (on-prem air-gapped installs)
Expose both sync and async iterator ergonomics to match existing SDK consumer patterns
Keep parser separate from hydration logic to enable reuse for TypeScript/Go SDKs later (shared spec for checkpoint markers)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: pydantic v2 strict parsing may reject slightly malformed model outputs -> mitigation: provide lenient parse mode and configurable field coerce rules
Risk: resume semantics could cause duplicate events -> mitigation: attach idempotency tokens and document at-most-once vs at-least-once behavior
Risk: increased memory footprint for buffering long sequences -> mitigation: dataclass path and configurable max_buffer_tokens limits
